chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Lunceford's Midwest and East dates, then the Audubon
summary: Over two months McRae travelled with Lunceford through the Midwest, then played the Audubon, Trenton and Washington.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: It seems that New York had a big activity there. With Lunceford, where else did you travel during this tow-month tenure?
Well we travelled all through the midwest like Cleveland, then Chicago and things like that.
Yeah, we played Indiana with him. And then we came on into (the East inaudible) and played --
I think we played the Audubon Ballroom one night {inaudible} --
up that night because the band had been on the road so long, you know. They came in from Buffalo and all the wives met the band (inaudible) and everything.
And the we went to Trenton. We left there after that playing that Sunday, we went to Trenton.
And we played the Audubon that Saturday night. And Sunday, we were supposed to play Trenton for two shows (inaudible) played there.
Then we went to Washington, D.C. Then we came back. By that time, it was the time that Joe met them back -- met them here in New York. And (inaudible).
I had a really good time.
You went back to the drawing board, so to speak?
I went back, yeah. Then I went back to writing again and doing gigging and things like that.
